strengths: Novel application of DRO to nodewise regression for variable clustering with clear connection to subspace clustering theory
Sound technical framework: Theorem 3.1 provides convex relaxation with factor-of-2 tightness; efficient ADMM algorithm with closed-form solutions (80% speedup vs CVX)
Data-driven parameter selection via Robust Wasserstein Profile (RWPI) with Theorem B.1 asymptotic guidance addresses key limitation of methods like SSC
Interpretable spectral norm regularization with clear robustness interpretation compared to L1 penalties
Comprehensive experiments with extensive ablations (Tables 8-10) and supplementary material demonstrating algorithmic robustness to initialization and parameter choices
weaknesses: No finite-sample cluster recovery guarantees despite assuming n→∞, d fixed; experiments violate this (n=250, d=500). No characterization of when clusters can be recovered
Factor-of-2 approximation in Theorem 3.1 is loose: replacing (γ-λᵢ)² with (γ-λ₁)² yields weak lower bound when eigenvalues cluster. This gap is unsatisfying and inadequately justified

Parameter selection methodology contradicts 'tuning-free' claims: requires choosing confidence level 1-α, estimating high-dimensional covariance Υ_g (requires d⁴ tensor or normality), and M=1000 MC samples. More complex than Lasso cross-validation

Unfair Lasso comparison: DRO uses sophisticated Theorem B.1 parameter selection while Lasso uses basic cross-validation. No analysis of optimally-tuned Lasso. Gaps could reflect tuning asymmetry rather than methodological superiority

Inconsistent and modest experimental results: Synthetic (0.92 vs 0.83 AMI) but Table 7 shows only marginal gains; Figure 6 shows near-identical performance under noise. Face clustering (0.58 AMI) lacks confidence intervals. Financial backtest lacks significance testing and baseline comparisons

Critical analyses missing: No cluster recovery conditions, failure modes, computational complexity O(·) analysis, scalability study, or principled guidance on when DRO outperforms alternatives. Why does SSC achieve 0.025 AMI (Table 1) vs 0.82 (Table 7)?

Financial application incomplete: Single backtest period (2001-2020), missing baseline comparisons (equal-weight, risk parity, 1/N), unclear if improvements come from clustering vs volatility selection vs low-risk anomaly, no statistical significance testing, heavy design choice dependence (K₁=K₂, annual updates)
